items.action: None. A subclass that declares its own `unslotted` no longer collides with ours.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class of yours that extends ModalComponent, ModalCardComponent or DrawerComponent. Template users need nothing; subclassing a DS component is unsupported.
items.verify: The app builds, and no subclass of ModalComponent, ModalCardComponent or DrawerComponent reads `this.unslotted`.
items.note: ModalComponent, ModalCardComponent and DrawerComponent each lost the private `unslotted`.

items.action:
Delete the `dsTooltipClippedLead` binding. Where it carried the host's own text, nothing replaces it. Where it carried other text, write it into the tooltip string as `'**' + lead + '**
' + tip`. A subclass of TooltipDirective that declared `dsTooltipClippedLead` has nothing to rename any more.
items.appliesWhen: Only an element that binds `dsTooltipClippedLead`, and a class that extends TooltipDirective. `dsTooltip`, `dsTooltipWhenClipped` and `dsTooltipTextSelector` are unchanged, and a `ds-table` header with a `hint` needs nothing.
items.pitfall: Deleting the binding drops the lead line where it was text other than the host's own; a clipped host leads with its own text in bold, never with a different one.
items.verify: No template or class binds `dsTooltipClippedLead`, the app compiles, and a clipped host that used it shows its text in bold above the tip.

items.action: None, unless a tooltip string holds `**` meant literally: write `\*\*` there.
items.appliesWhen: Every `dsTooltip` string, including one a component builds from data. `dsTooltipWhenClipped` with no `dsTooltip` shows the host's text as written and is unaffected.
items.pitfall: A string with two `**` loses both and the text between them turns bold, with no error; user-supplied text reaching a tooltip needs its `**` escaped.
items.verify: Every tooltip string whose text contains `**` shows the asterisks, or bold where bold was meant.

items.action: None. To keep one tooltip from repeating the host's text, include that text in its `dsTooltip` string.
items.appliesWhen: A host with `dsTooltip` or `dsTooltipWhenClipped` that shows less text than it holds and whose tip does not already contain that text. A host that fits, and a tip that already contains the host's text, read as before.
items.pitfall: A screenshot of a clipped button or label with a tooltip gains a bold first line.
items.verify: Narrow a button or label that has a `dsTooltip` until it clips and open the tooltip: its text is bold on the first line, the tip below.

items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename a member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class of yours that extends TooltipDirective, TooltipPanelComponent or BarChartComponent. Template users of dsTooltip and ds-bar-chart need nothing; subclassing a DS component is unsupported.
items.pitfall: A redeclared private member collides as a public one does, and override cannot resolve it; only a rename does.
items.verify: The app builds with no member-collision error against TooltipDirective, TooltipPanelComponent or BarChartComponent.
items.note: TooltipPanelComponent gained 2: the protected segments and the public arrow. TooltipDirective gained 3: the private contains and ownText and the public dsTooltipArrow; it lost dsTooltipClippedLead. BarChartComponent gained the public labelPosition, the protected isExpanded, toggleRow, hintId, holdsControls, percentColumn, entries, showsSkeleton and reloading, and the private idPrefix and expanded.

items.action: None, unless your code builds a complete DsIntl object of its own: add chart.rowsUnder, the name of a bar-chart group's disclosure button.
items.appliesWhen: Only an object or signal typed as the full DsIntl, not as DsIntlOverrides. provideDsIntl with a partial override, and every app that leaves DS_INTL alone, is unaffected.
items.pitfall: An object that spreads DS_INTL_DEFAULTS.chart compiles, but a chart section written out key by key without the spread fails with TS2741 on rowsUnder.
items.verify: The app builds, and every complete DsIntl object it declares has chart.rowsUnder.

items.action: None, unless a screen relies on the skeleton replacing rows that are already drawn: bind data to an empty array while loading is set.
items.appliesWhen: Only a ds-bar-chart whose loading is set while its data still holds rows, such as a reload or a filter change. A first load with empty data still draws skeleton rows.
items.pitfall: A test or screenshot that waits for the skeleton after a reload no longer finds it: the drawn rows stay, inert under the overlay, until loading clears.
items.verify: A ds-bar-chart reloading with rows on screen shows those rows under a scrim and spinner, and one loading with empty data shows skeleton rows.

informational.text: A `<div actions>` (or `<div drawer-footer>`) wrapper in the footer of `ds-modal`, `ds-modal-card`, `ds-drawer` and `ds-bottom-sheet` gets `display: contents` at zero specificity, so its buttons take the footer's gap, alignment and `ds-modal-card` stacking. A `display` set on the wrapper in your own styles still wins.
informational.verify: Open a dialog, drawer or bottom sheet whose buttons sit in a `<div actions>` and confirm they are spaced like buttons that carry `actions` themselves, not touching.

informational: `ds-modal`, `ds-modal-card` and `ds-drawer` no longer warn in dev mode about content without a slot, or about an attribute that names no slot. That content still renders in the body. A test or screenshot that waited for the `Dev warning` toast these raised has nothing to wait for.

ds-bar-chart takes labelPosition ('top' | 'start', default 'top', type BarChartLabelPosition): 'start' puts each label in a column before its bar and aligns labels, bars, values and percents across rows. --ds-bar-chart-label-column-max-width caps the label column. Under 'start', --ds-bar-chart-row-gap defaults to var(--space-3) instead of var(--space-5); set --ds-bar-chart-row-gap: var(--space-5) to keep the wider rhythm. A chart left on 'top' keeps var(--space-5).

BarChartRow takes children (rows nested behind a disclosure button, each measured against its parent's value), hint (a defined-term label with a tooltip), emphasis (a bold label), showPercent (a per-row override of the chart's showPercent) and detached (a row set apart by a divider and given no partOfWhole share). --ds-bar-chart-child-fill-opacity and --ds-bar-chart-divider-color style the new rows. A chart without these fields renders as before.

informational.text: A ds-bar-chart whose data has any hint or children renders its rows container with role="group" instead of role="img", so the disclosure and term buttons inside it stay reachable to assistive technology; a chart without them keeps role="img".
informational.verify: Open a bar chart with a hinted or grouped row and confirm Tab reaches the term and the disclosure button, and that a screen reader announces the term's hint.

informational: A ds-bar-chart row whose value is NaN, Infinity, or a [low, high] pair with a non-finite end shows — for its value, its derived percentage and its partOfWhole share instead of 0 and 0.0%, and draws no bar; an explicit percent on the row still prints. The generated summary leaves such a row out of its lowest and highest readings.

informational.text: ds-bar-chart skeleton rows use the drawn row markup: a label, value and percent placeholder and a placeholder filling the track, so each skeleton row is as tall as a drawn row and the track keeps its height and cap. Under labelPosition 'start' the placeholder label column takes --ds-bar-chart-label-column-max-width, because no label text exists yet to size it.
informational.verify: Open a ds-bar-chart with loading and empty data, then give it rows, and confirm the rows land where the skeleton rows were.

informational: ds-loading-overlay takes --ds-loading-overlay-radius (default 0) for the corners of its scrim; set it to the radius of the container the overlay covers.

informational.text: A bordered ds-table's reload overlay rounds its bottom corners to the table's radius (--ds-table-radius, else --ds-radius-control) instead of ending square outside the rounded border.
informational.verify: Open a bordered ds-table with rows and loading set, and confirm the scrim's bottom corners follow the table's rounded border.

informational.text: A reloading ds-bar-chart covers the whole card with the overlay, to the frame's rounded corners, instead of a scrim over the rows inside the padding.
informational.verify: Open a framed ds-bar-chart with rows and loading set, and confirm the blurred scrim reaches the card's edges and corners.
